bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege environment API-key holder can send PUT /api/v1/runs/:runId/metadata with an operation such as {type:"set",key:"$.__proto__.polluted",value:"PWNED"}. UpdateMetadataRequestBody accepted operation.key as an unrestricted string and applyMetadataOperations passed the path to @jsonhero/path without rejecting __proto__, constructor, or prototype. JSONHeroPath.set therefore writes through __proto__ to Object.prototype in the shared webapp process. Inherited attacker data then contaminates unrelated Prisma and prom-client objects across tenants, breaking worker authentication and allowing a repeatable process-wide denial of service.
flaw_origin: The public main-line commit 34f8bd588e6f1a3edcf3aac3c773d3a0e35af4bf is a GitHub squash of PR #1563. Its reconstructable PR branch has the same final tree, and the smallest member that first adds the unrestricted operation schemas, the operations endpoint path, and JSONHeroPath(operation.key).set is cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d ("Implement run metadata updates from ancestor tasks").
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d` records human author and committer Eric Allam <eallam@icloud.com>, a GitButler change-id header, and only the subject `Implement run metadata updates from ancestor tasks`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party GHSA-p28v-f755-9qrg documents the authenticated PUT attack, `$.__proto__.polluted` proof, cross-tenant Prisma/prom-client effects, advisory range >=3.3.8 through 4.5.5, and patched version 4.5.6. In the validated clone, `git log --all -S'new JSONHeroPath(operation.key)' -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` returns the public squash 34f8bd588e6f1a3edcf3aac3c773d3a0e35af4bf and its branch member cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d. `git log -L 20,27:packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d` attributes the first `new JSONHeroPath(operation.key)` and `path.set(newMetadata, operation.value)` lines to cf80. `git show cf80 -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts packages/core/src/v3/schemas/common.ts apps/webapp/app/services/metadata/updateMetadata.server.ts` shows that same commit creates the helper, defines every keyed operation with z.string(), and routes request-body operations into it. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 229707951c66c6796a2ed6ca75872545df9a60c4 -- packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` prints nothing, while `git show 229707951c66c6796a2ed6ca75872545df9a60c4:packages/core/src/v3/schemas/common.ts` has none of the operation schemas, directly proving parent absence. PR #1563 reports head ad5a3db013086ecb401b36695219d8bd7a835c1e; both it and squash 34f resolve to tree 8dad287dc514d1ec773829ba88e8fb92ef28ab0c, proving the decomposition. `git show cf80:packages/core/package.json` reports package version 3.3.8 and @jsonhero/path ^1.0.21, matching the advisory's lower boundary; repository release tags are slightly different operational evidence: @trigger.dev/core@3.3.8 points to pre-BIC 4243cb2451ebe4c892591f1d0439358c84286988, while the first containing core tag is @trigger.dev/core@3.3.9 at efd61f1374c44eb94b2776dbaaceb2346db9b22c. For closure, `git show 0c2d9ce22a1af5e2ae8d1809cba38051b4acfb1a` shows the focused security-branch change adding isSafeMetadataKey, schema refinements, and a runtime guard that rejects dangerous segments. `git log --reverse cc748422d8188833948035281cc50ef4f7ab77e2..fc392b1fcaa0b929ead6ff8caef2e160f782109e` places 0c2 in PR #4316's security branch; fc392 and public squash 6997 both resolve to tree 73eea7370b72f9e966c5ec0378cec52cf5db89ae. `git tag --contains 6997 --list 'v4.5.*' --sort=version:refname` starts at v4.5.6, and direct `git show v4.5.5:packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts` versus v4.5.6 shows the former unguarded and the latter guarded.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires both attacker-controlled metadata operation keys and an unsafe path setter; cf80 is the first atomic branch commit that adds that complete causal chain. The later 34f public commit is only a squash representation of cf80 plus unrelated PR members, so treating 34f as the BIC would violate the smallest-real-BIC rule. The immediate cf80 parent lacks both the helper file and operation schemas, and -S/-L independently converge on cf80. The focused fix is 0c2; the advisory-linked 6997 is the public security-release squash that contains it, with v4.5.5/v4.5.6 proving the closing tag boundary. AI attribution is judged only from cf80's raw commit object, which has a human identity and no qualifying AI marker; CodeRabbit activity on the PR and AI-related repository dependencies are outside the BIC commit-object rule and do not change the result.
